messages.subject: Lavaan Warnings with SEM
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to fit a latent factor model in R using Lavaan package. I am new to R ( I do have some experiences with SEM in Amos), but I am not yet at the point that I truly understand why some of these warnings are being prompted and how to solve them. I get the below stated warnings: 

Warning messages:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

2: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

If I read my output I am able to understand the origin of the second warning (covariance between ODev and WE is negative,see the last part of the output), but I am not sure how to solve this as the indicators of these latent factors seem fine.

The first warning is the one that I truly have no clue as to where it originates from.

If anyone here can help me understand these warnings I will be very grateful!!

EDIT: I am sorry if this question has been posted before. I have searched this forum, but I could not find an answer that solved my problem.

Jason--
    I think the core of your identification problem (which is probably the source of the "can't estimate standard errors" warning) is in your structural model:

+ #Regressions
+   OInno ~ WE + EIS
+   ODev ~ WE + EIS
+ #Intercepts
+ #Variances
+   WE ~~ EIS + OInno + ODev + Stra + Ven
+   EIS ~~ OInno + ODev + Stra + Ven

You have WE and EIS predicted by OInno and ODev, but then you allow WE and EIS to share residual covariance with OInno and ODev.  That makes your structural model nonrecursive and raises potential identification issues.  If you did not allow these particular residual covariances, then I think your identification problem would disappear.  If you want to retain these residual covariances, then you are going to need to learn something about identification.
     I don't know whether the negative residual covariances are related to the "not positive definite" message.  Covariances can certainly be negative--though one badly placed negative in a covariance matrix can certainly make a matrix not positive definite.
--Ed Rigdon
